line: I’m with a hundred and fifty steppers, I’m with Swerve
vault_lines: I'm with a hundred and fifty steppers, I'm with Swerve
meaning:
Alongside G Herbo (or Swerve), Skilla suggests he’s with 150 steppers—people who would shoot on his behalf if he gives them the word. However, the number 150 is a purposeful allusion to G Herbo and the fact that he’s collaborating with Skilla on this song. This bar is a reference to 150 Dream Team, a record label imprint Herb started after joining Cinematic Music Group and partnering with Machine Entertainment Group in September 2015.

The 150 Dream Team label imprint has been listed as a copyright holder on a large majority of Herbo’s musical catalog and their Instagram page handles G Herbo’s official merchandise.

line: You thought Doe Boy was one of us, we jump out minivans (Uh)
vault_lines: You thought Doe Boy was one of us, we jump out minivans (Uh)
meaning:
Herbo proclaims that you could confuse rapper Doe Boy for a gang member in Chicago despite him being from Ohio because Herbo and his crew jump out of minivans, presumably when breaking the law. This is because the 2018 track “Mini Vans” was one of Doe Boy’s breakout hits after signing with Future’s Freebandz label. On the track, Doe Boy raps:

You better run Forrest, run Forrest, run
‘Cause them niggas slide in mini vans where I’m from

Doe Boy has previously collaborated with Skilla on songs like 2023’s “Smack Sh*t” and 2024’s “Special.” He also has songs with G Herbo like 2022’s “OPP PARTY” and “SET IT OFF.”

line: Like he discovered Young Buck, done fucked up many men
vault_lines: Like he discovered Young Buck, done fucked up many men
meaning:
G Herbo is describing how his big cuz—mentioned four lines earlier has “fucked up,” or injured several of his enemies. The Chicago native is comparing him to New York rapper 50 Cent, who notably has a major hit song released in 2003 titled, “Many Men (Wish Death)” which Herbo name-drops at the end of the bar. Furthermore, 50 is also known for signing rapper Young Buck to his G-Unit record label in 2003—tying together this 50 Cent reference, as he is the person who Herbo associates with discovering Young Buck, as well as alluding to one of his most popular tracks.

Interestingly enough, G Herbo went on to allude to both of the aforementioned artists on his late 2024 track, “Yup” with this bar:

Wasn’t even worryin' ‘bout 50 Cent
Young, hit niggas with them buck, buck, buck, buck, buck, buck
